title: Strict planar L2 Rogers-Shephard inequality for centrally symmetric hexagons
statement: Let K be a two-dimensional centrally symmetric convex polygon with exactly six vertices and with 0 in K. For p=2, |K op_2 (-K)| is strictly less than (2+pi/2)|K|, for every allowed location of the origin in K.
claim: No genuine centrally symmetric hexagon is an equality case of Corollary 29 at p=2. At a vertex translation, after affine normalization by three zonotope generators e1, e2, and (r,s) with r,s>0, half of the sharp-bound deficit equals pi*r-2(r-s)*atan(r/s), which is strictly positive; translation shadow-system convexity extends strictness to every origin placement.
contribution: An exact classification of the minimal non-parallelogram centrally symmetric polygon family at p=2, obtained by closed normal-fan integration rather than finite enumeration.
dependencies: The standard representation of a centrally symmetric hexagon as a three-generator zonotope.
Translation shadow-system convexity as used in the second proof of Corollary 29 of arXiv:2607.03582v1.
limitations: The original conjecture remains unresolved for centrally symmetric bodies with more than six polygonal vertices or nonpolygonal boundary.
The claim is only for p=2 and does not address other p>1.
The limited literature search is not a priority claim, and the exact argument has not yet received fresh referee audit.
